title: Nehru and Albert Einstein: The Quest for Nuclear Sanity
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: Einstein and Nehru discussed nuclear disarmament, with Einstein affirming that Gandhi's non-violence was humanity's sole defense against atomic self-destruction.
keywords: Nehru and Albert Einstein: The Quest for Nuclear Sanity
full_text:
On November 5, 1949, at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey, two visionary minds conversed in private: Albert Einstein and Jawaharlal Nehru.

Tormented by the atomic devastation of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Einstein had dedicated his final years to anti-war activism.

Clasping Nehru's hand, Einstein asked with deep earnestness:
"Prime Minister Nehru, the superpowers are escalating an insane nuclear arms race. Atomic weapons threaten the biological extinction of mankind! Is there any hope for the survival of human civilization?"

Nehru answered with serene conviction:
"Professor Einstein! Our master Mahatma Gandhi taught us that 'An eye for an eye only ends up making the whole world blind.'
No military victory is possible in a nuclear war. India will never align with military blocs. We choose the path of Non-Alignment, advocating peaceful coexistence (*Panchsheel*) and universal disarmament!"

Einstein's face radiated relief:
"Prime Minister, Gandhi was the only statesman of our age who showed the world that moral power is superior to military force!
Science has enlightened the human intellect, but only Gandhi's non-violence can educate the human heart!
May India hold aloft this moral beacon for all humanity!"

Their dialogue stands as an eternal monument to the alliance between scientific reason and moral conscience.
moral: Technological power devoid of moral wisdom leads to catastrophe; ethical courage must govern the tools of science.
witty_quote: Science has granted man godlike power; only Gandhian ethics can save humanity from its own suicidal impulses!
